```{r}
# c/ Cattell-Nelson-Gorsuch indices
# CNG scree test

m <- nFactors::nCng(df2[,2:length(df2)], cor = TRUE, model = "factors", details = TRUE)
print(m) #nCng() finds the largest k such that the first k eigenvalues are “significantly” above random.
nf <- m$nFactors  

eig_df <- data.frame(
  Factor = seq_along(m$detail$values),
  Eigenvalue = m$detail$values
)

eig_df$highlight <- eig_df$Factor <= nf

eig_df$Factor <= nf 

ggplot(eig_df, aes(x = Factor, y = Eigenvalue, color = highlight)) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  geom_line(color = "black") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey") +
  labs(title = "Scree Plot of Eigenvalues",x = "Factor Number",y = "Eigenvalue") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 16)+theme(aspect.ratio = 1)+ scale_color_manual(values = c("#66D9FF","#ff00ff58"))


plotuScree(df2[,2:length(df2)], main=paste(m$nFactors," factors retained by the CNG procedure",sep=""))
```


```{r}
# d/ Multiple Regression Procedure
#computes the β indices, like their associated Student t and probability (Zoski and Jurs, 1993, 1996, p. 445). These three values can be used as three different indices for determining the number of components/factors to retain.
# https://rdrr.io/cran/nFactors/man/nMreg.html
m <- nMreg(df2[,2:length(df2)], cor = TRUE, model = "factors", details = TRUE)
print(m)
mdf <- data.frame(m$detail)
plotuScree(df2[,2:length(df2)], main=paste(m$nFactors[1], ", ",
                            m$nFactors[2], " or ",
                            m$nFactors[3],
                            " factors retained by the MREG procedures",
                            sep=""))
```

### Sample size adequacy: communalities and items per factor (Mundfrom et al., 2005)
```{r}
# Mundfrom, Shaw & Ke (2005) tabulate the minimum N for good (congruence .92) / excellent (.98) recovery
# as a function of number of factors, variables-to-factors ratio (p/f) and communality level:
# high = .6-.8, wide = .2-.8, low = .2-.4. Above p/f ~ 6 the required N stabilises.
n_used <- sum(complete.cases(df2[,2:length(df2)]))
L <- unclass(fa3$loadings)
p <- nrow(L)
h2 <- fa3$communality

summary(h2)
table(cut(h2, breaks = c(0, .2, .4, .6, .8, 1), include.lowest = TRUE))

# communality level: where at least 80% of the items fall
h2_level <- if (mean(h2 >= .6) >= .8) "high" else if (mean(h2 >= .2 & h2 <= .4) >= .8) "low" else "wide"

# items per factor: by primary loading and by salient loading (|loading| >= .40)
primary <- factor(colnames(L)[apply(abs(L), 1, which.max)], levels = colnames(L))
items_per_factor <- data.frame(
  primary = as.vector(table(primary)),
  salient = colSums(abs(L) >= .40),
  row.names = colnames(L)
)
items_per_factor

data.frame(
  N = n_used,
  items = p,
  factors = nFactors,
  N_per_item = round(n_used / p, 1),
  pf_ratio = round(p / nFactors, 1),
  pf_ratio_min = min(items_per_factor$primary),
  mean_h2 = round(mean(h2), 2),
  h2_level = h2_level
)

mundfrom_minN <- NA
if (!is.na(mundfrom_minN)) n_used >= mundfrom_minN
```


### Subsampling stability check
```{r}
set.seed(123) 

fractions <- c(.6, .7, .8, .9)
n_rep <- 100

# get ppt and full sample loadings
items_cc <- df2[complete.cases(df2[,2:length(df2)]), 2:length(df2)]
L_full <- unclass(fa3$loadings)

# match factors full and subsample based on best fit
perms <- expand.grid(rep(list(1:nFactors), nFactors))
perms <- as.matrix(perms[apply(perms, 1, function(r) length(unique(r)) == nFactors), ])

match_congruence <- function(L_sub, L_ref) {
  # Tucker congruence between every pair of factors;
  cc <- abs(factor.congruence(L_sub, L_ref))
  scores <- apply(perms, 1, function(pr) sum(cc[cbind(pr, 1:nFactors)]))
  best <- perms[which.max(scores), ]
  # return one congruence per full-sample factor, in the order of L_ref's columns (ML1, ML2, ML3)
  cc[cbind(best, 1:nFactors)]
}

#sample
sub_res <- list()
for (f in fractions) {
  n_sub <- round(f * nrow(items_cc))
  for (i in 1:n_rep) {
    # draw n_sub participants at random
    sub <- items_cc[sample(nrow(items_cc), n_sub), ]
    # item correlation matrix of the subsample
    R_sub <- suppressWarnings(cor(sub, method = corr_type))
    if (any(is.na(R_sub))) next  # item without variance skipped
    
    # refit the same model as fa3: same number of factors, ML extraction, oblimin rotation
    fit <- tryCatch(suppressWarnings(suppressMessages(fa(R_sub, nfactors = nFactors, rotate = "oblimin", fm = "ml"))),
                    error = function(e) NULL)
    if (is.null(fit)) next
    sub_res[[length(sub_res) + 1]] <- data.frame(fraction = f, n = n_sub, factor = colnames(L_full),
                                                 congruence = match_congruence(unclass(fit$loadings), L_full))
  }
}
sub_res <- bind_rows(sub_res)

# Summary per subsample size and factor
# n_fits  = number of successful fits (out of n_rep)
# mean    = average congruence with the full-sample factor

sub_summary <- sub_res %>%
  group_by(fraction, n, factor) %>%
  summarise(n_fits = n(),
            mean = mean(congruence),
            q05 = quantile(congruence, .05),
            prop_95 = mean(congruence > .95),
            prop_85 = mean(congruence > .85),
            .groups = "drop")
sub_summary


```

```{r}

# mean congruence per factor against subsample size;
# dashed lines mark the .85 and .95 thresholds.
ggplot(sub_summary, aes(x = fraction, y = mean, color = factor)) +
  geom_line() + geom_point() +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = q05, ymax = mean), width = 0.02) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(.85, .95), linetype = "dashed", color = "grey") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = fractions, labels = paste0(fractions * 100, "%")) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(ML1 = "#E6A3EE", ML2 = "#91316D", ML3 = "grey50"),
                     breaks = c("ML2", "ML1", "ML3"),
                     labels = c("Anxious-Depression", "IoU-Worry", "Well-being")) +
  labs(x = "Subsample size (% of full sample)", y = "Tucker congruence with full sample", color = "Factor") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 16) + theme(aspect.ratio = 1)

```




### Item correlation matrix with factor loadings (as in Gillan et al., 2016, Figure 3)
```{r gillan_fig, fig.width = 12, fig.height = 11}
library(cowplot)

# one factor per side of the matrix: top, left, right
fac_order  <- c("ML2", "ML1", "ML3")
fac_labels <- c("Anxious-Depression", "IoU-Worry", "Well-being")

# loadings and item correlation matrix (cdf was overwritten above, so recompute)
L_fig <- unclass(fa3$loadings)[, fac_order]
R_items <- cor(df2[, 2:length(df2)], method = corr_type, use = "complete.obs")
subscale_fig <- fa3.load$subscale_pure[match(rownames(L_fig), fa3.load$varname)]

# order items by primary factor, then subscale, then absolute loading within subscale
prim <- factor(fac_order[apply(abs(L_fig), 1, which.max)], levels = fac_order)
item_order <- rownames(L_fig)[order(prim, subscale_fig, -apply(abs(L_fig), 1, max))]

# long format for the heatmap
heat_df <- reshape2::melt(R_items[item_order, item_order], varnames = c("item1", "item2"), value.name = "r")
heat_df$item1 <- factor(heat_df$item1, levels = item_order)
heat_df$item2 <- factor(heat_df$item2, levels = rev(item_order))

# loadings with subscale for colouring
load_df <- data.frame(item = rownames(L_fig), subscale_pure = subscale_fig, L_fig)

# minimal loading axis (-0.5, 0, 0.5); the item axis is hidden in each panel
load_breaks <- c(-0.5, 0, 0.5)
theme_margin <- theme_classic() +
  theme(axis.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"), legend.position = "none")
hide_x <- theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(), axis.ticks.x = element_blank(), axis.line.x = element_blank())
hide_y <- theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank(), axis.line.y = element_blank())

# centre: item x item correlation matrix
p_heat <- ggplot(heat_df, aes(x = item1, y = item2, fill = r)) +
  geom_raster() +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2166AC", mid = "white", high = "#B2182B", limits = c(-1, 1), name = "r") +
  scale_x_discrete(expand = c(0, 0)) + scale_y_discrete(expand = c(0, 0)) +
  theme_void() + theme(legend.position = "none")

# colour bar for the correlations, placed under the matrix at its full width
p_rbar <- ggplot(data.frame(r = seq(-1, 1, length.out = 201)), aes(x = r, y = 1, fill = r)) +
  geom_raster() +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2166AC", mid = "white", high = "#B2182B", limits = c(-1, 1)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(-1, 1, 0.5), expand = c(0, 0)) + scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(x = "Correlation (r)", y = NULL) + theme_margin + hide_y + theme(axis.line.x = element_blank())

# top: Anxious-Depression loadings (columns aligned with the matrix)
p_top <- ggplot(load_df %>% mutate(item = factor(item, levels = item_order)),
                aes(x = item, y = ML2, fill = subscale_pure)) +
  geom_col(width = 1) + geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.2) +
  scale_x_discrete(expand = c(0, 0)) + scale_y_continuous(breaks = load_breaks) + expand_limits(y = load_breaks) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = custom_colors) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = fac_labels[1]) + theme_margin + hide_x

# left: IoU-Worry loadings (rows aligned with the matrix), bars growing away from the matrix
p_left <- ggplot(load_df %>% mutate(item = factor(item, levels = rev(item_order))),
                 aes(x = ML1, y = item, fill = subscale_pure)) +
  geom_col(width = 1) + geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.2) +
  scale_y_discrete(expand = c(0, 0)) + scale_x_reverse(breaks = load_breaks) + expand_limits(x = load_breaks) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = custom_colors) +
  labs(x = fac_labels[2], y = NULL) + theme_margin + hide_y

# right: Well-being loadings (rows aligned with the matrix), bars growing away from the matrix
p_right <- ggplot(load_df %>% mutate(item = factor(item, levels = rev(item_order))),
                  aes(x = ML3, y = item, fill = subscale_pure)) +
  geom_col(width = 1) + geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.2) +
  scale_y_discrete(expand = c(0, 0)) + scale_x_continuous(breaks = load_breaks) + expand_limits(x = load_breaks) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = custom_colors) +
  labs(x = fac_labels[3], y = NULL) + theme_margin + hide_y

# subscale legend placed separately so the panels keep the same size and stay aligned
subscale_legend <- get_plot_component(
  p_top + theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
    guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 3, title = "Subscale", title.position = "top")),
  "guide-box-bottom", return_all = TRUE)

plot_grid(
  plot_grid(NULL, p_top, NULL, p_left, p_heat, p_right, NULL, p_rbar, NULL, ncol = 3, align = "hv", axis = "tblr",
            rel_widths = c(1, 3, 1), rel_heights = c(1, 3, 0.45)),
  subscale_legend,
  ncol = 1, rel_heights = c(1, 0.15)
)
```
